\caption{\textbf{Near-equal aggregate accuracy does not certify interchangeable behavior.} One registered cell: Qwen2.5-7B on GSM8K, 4-bit GPTQ against 4-bit AWQ, paired on byte-identical calibration samples across five seeds. (A)~The two methods differ by 0.58~pp of aggregate accuracy. (B)~The same items disagree far more than that: 9.12\% of items go from correct to wrong and 8.54\% from wrong to correct, so the aggregate gap is the small difference between two large opposing quantities whose sum is 17.66\%. (C)~At the observed disagreement rate, certifying equivalence at a declared $\pm2$~pp margin would need 2{,}730 items against the 1{,}000 run. That is a planning requirement computed at an assumed true difference of zero: it says the evaluation cannot support the claim, not that the methods differ. (D)~The sign of the difference changes with the calibration draw alone, and across the eight registered cells the winner reverses in 5 of 8. \textbf{Scope.} This cell is an illustrative example chosen because it is legible, and it is the most extreme of the eight: its churn-to-net-delta ratio is $30.4\times$ against a median of $12.7\times$ across the eight. All eight are shown in~(D) for that reason. The atlas figures in the panel above are observational and describe the public evaluation record rather than a census of compression.}
\label{fig:cancellation}
